It looks like casting has nearly turned into mission impossible.

Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult have emerged as potential contenders for the role of James Bond in the upcoming 007 film, according to Variety.

Both actors were among those who have reportedly screen tested for the coveted role.

The race to find the next James Bond has been a competitive one, as Pattinson and Hoult are just two out of many names who have been rumored to have been auditioning.

Page Six previously reported that other finalists included actors Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor. Harry Styles and Theo James have also had discussions about the role, according to Variety.

Amazon declined to comment when reached via email by Page Six on Saturday morning.

The new movie, developed by Amazon MGM studios, is slated for a 2028 release. Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the upcoming film.

Earlier this week, it was rumored that “The Crown” actor O’Connell had already landed the part, after one of his loose-lipped “Golden Boy” cast members reportedly spilled the beans during a night out at a London pub.

entertainment.title: 10 TV Shows To Watch If You Like Percy Jackson And The Olympians
entertainment.summary: Ancient myths, young heroes, and adventures come together in these fantasy and sci-fi shows, offering new worlds for fans of Percy Jackson And The Olympians.
entertainment.body:
Disney+ Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover For teens growing up in the late 2000s or early 2010s, reading the "Percy Jackson & the Olympians" novels was practically a rite of passage, especially for those obsessed with Greek mythology. It's only a shame it took nearly two decades for a faithful adaptation to hit TV with the Disney+ series of the same name. The series follows the adventures of the titular teen (Walker Scobell), who discovers he's the demigod son of Poseidon (Toby Stephens) after arriving at Camp Half-Blood, a training ground for young demigods.

With lots of Easter eggs that fans of Greek mythology will love, and a star-studded cast that includes Jason Mantzoukas, Lin-Manuel Miranda, and Kate McKinnon as Olympian gods, "Percy Jackson and the Olympians" returns for Season 3 on November 20. The wait between seasons can be grueling for fans, and those who've already read the books dozens of times might want something new to obsess over in the coming months.

Thankfully, these 10 shows are practically tailor-made for fans of the "Percy Jackson" franchise, even with some of them predating the first book's release. From lore-filled adventure series and coming-of-age fantasy shows, there may not be Greek gods in every one of these shows, but their diversity and appeal to all ages will certainly satisfy anyone who's been enjoying the mythological chaos of Disney+'s latest hit.

Netflix Kicking things off with the most overtly Greek mythology-based show on this list, "Blood of Zeus" is tonally quite a far cry from "Percy Jackson and the Olympians." However, the two shows have more in common than simply including the Hellenistic deities and mythos. "Blood of Zeus," like "Percy Jackson," follows the demigod son of an Olympian; in this case, Heron (Derek Phillips), son of Zeus (Jason O'Mara). However, its interpretations of various figures from Greek mythology often skew darker than those in the mainly family-friendly Disney+ series.

When the series begins, Heron is a lot like Percy Jackson, having no idea about his true parentage and living a rather modest life before being thrust into a war against an army of demons. Mentored by his disguised father and allied with the Amazonian warrior Alexia (Jessica Henwick), Heron sets out to save humanity, drawing the ire of vengeful gods like Hera (Claudia Christian) and Ares (Matt Lowe).

Although it forges a new narrative in Greek mythology rather than replaying certain iconic stories like "Percy Jackson & the Olympians" does, "Blood of Zeus" might be one of the strongest additions to Greek mythology-based fiction of all time. Even its stunning, gritty animated visuals hold a candle to the best fantasy shows on TV, drawing comparisons to "Game of Thrones" and "Castlevania," among others. That being said, its graphic violence and mature content make it a better recommendation for older "Percy Jackson" fans.

entertainment.title: 5 Times Gibbs Broke His Own Rules On NCIS
entertainment.summary: Gibbs' famous rules on "NCIS" generally serve him and the team, but on a few occasions, even the Special Agent himself couldn't help but break them.
entertainment.body:
CBS Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Beginning in 2003, Mark Harman guided audiences through the world of naval special investigations as Leroy Jethro Gibbs on the CBS crime show "NCIS." In a vast world of procedural crime dramas, "NCIS" stands out with its focus on crimes involving the Navy and Marine Corps, as the acronym stands for Naval Criminal Investigative Services. There's a reason it's still one of the most streamed TV shows of 2026 . For 18 full seasons, Gibbs led his team through events like terrorist explosions, and the murder of their director. His competence and talent as a leading military investigator was largely owed to the set of personal rules Gibbs holds both his team and himself to . As the saying goes, however, rules were made to be broken.

For all his strengths and virtues, Gibbs was not always able to follow the rules that helped shape his personality. Sometimes he had to break them to solve the case, while other times it was more personal. Regardless of his reasons for doing so, there were at least five times Gibbs broke his own rules.

CBS In Season 8's "Ships in the Night," The team is investigating the murder of a Marine officer whose family operated a radar company. The victim's sister Kimberly Nolan (Tiffany Dupont), their family lawyer Wayne Grossman (Roark Critchlow), and the company CFO Tom Adams (Patch Darragh) are Gibbs' suspects. He decides to break his first rule by placing the three suspects together in a conference room. After cleverly exposing a bullet graze wound on Kimberly's arm, she breaks down and claims the other two forced her to lead her brother to his death. This prompts all of them to turn on each other, culminating in Wayne pulling out an audio recording of Tom and Kimberly conspiring to commit the crime.

By actively breaking his own rule about placing suspects together, Gibbs forces so much pressure on them that he gains a confession, enabling him to close the case. Fortunately, this is a positive example of his disregard to his own system, which has defined his character since the beginning of the series.

CBS In the 20th episode of Season 16, the bones of Gibbs' ex-fiancé Ellen Wallace (Erin Cummings) are found inside a Marine Corps uniform by a construction crew. It was previously believed that Wallace died during the 9/11 terrorist attacks. Blood on the uniform gets matched with Gibbs, who claims that she had simply cleaned up a cut he sustained with her uniform. Because of this history, he is removed from the case.

entertainment.title: Elvis Presley Rights Owners Sue Suno Over AI Voice Cloning: ‘Elvis’ Identity Was Stolen’
entertainment.summary: The singer's legendary voice is at the center of a cutting-edge lawsuit that aims to hold the AI firm legally liable for allowing users to create knockoff vocals.
entertainment.body:
The owners of Elvis Presley ’s intellectual property are suing Suno in a new lawsuit that claims the artificial intelligence music company violated the King of Rock ‘n’ Roll’s likeness rights by stealing his voice.

The new lawsuit marks one of the first major cases under a new Tennessee law, coincidentally called the ELVIS Act, that was recently enacted to address problems caused by AI. The first-in-the-nation statute was touted as a weapon against people who create illegal deepfakes, but it also allows for lawsuits against tech firms that enable such voice and image cloning in the first place.

Friday’s lawsuit was filed by Elvis Presley Enterprises, a unit of the licensing giant Authentic Brands Group that controls the intellectual property tied to Elvis, including much of his song catalog and the rights to his name, image and likeness. In a statement to Billboard on Saturday, ABG spokeswoman Lark-Marie Antón said the new lawsuit and its evidence “speak for themselves.”

“The name, image, likeness, and music of Elvis Presley are among the most valuable intellectual property assets in the world,” Antón said. “We protect those rights vigorously.”

A spokeswoman for Suno did not immediately return a request for comment on Saturday.

The looming battle with Suno will raise untested legal questions about the extent to which AI companies can be sued for allegedly ripping off a musical artist’s identity. The use of AI to convincingly mimic real people has been one of the booming technology’s most controversial applications, and no where less so than an industry largely built on famous singing voices.

“Elvis’ voice possessed a distinctively rich vocal timbre, with a warm velvety resonance and perfectly employed vibrato, coupled with his ability to vary his technique and delivery within the same song as well as across several different styles of music, which became his immediately recognizable musical signature across the world,” the lawsuit says.

Suno has argued in other lawsuits that its current models do not allow users to include the names of specific artists in prompts, nor produce outputs that mimic specific real voices. But in Friday’s complaint, the Elvis owners say those claims are “unequivocally false.” They included links to videos capturing the use of Suno’s platform to play songs that sound remarkably similar to Presley.

entertainment.title: ‘7th Heaven’ star Jeremy London refutes claims that he is ‘homeless,’ fires back at celebrity news reporters: ‘Stupid’
entertainment.summary: The actor sparked concern among fans on Thursday after taking to X to ask for help finding work and housing.
entertainment.body:
Jeremy London is denying claims that he is “homeless” following headlines about his plea for help finding work and housing.

London, best known for his role as Chandler Hampton on family drama series “7th Heaven,” took to X on Friday to specifically call out People’s coverage of his since-deleted post about his personal situation.

“Guys … I have a condo in Florida. People mag out here making me look homeless 😂🤣,” London, 54, wrote. “I was just in shock from by [sic] boss’ behavior and didn’t want to have to go back to Florida. Jesus, they really have nothing else to report on 🥴.”

Less than an hour later, he seemingly took another swipe at celebrity news outlets in general: “Being a celebrity of any kind is so stupid. Our tweets should not be news. 😂.”

The “Party of Five” actor also appeared to reassure fans that he was doing OK, responding in the comment section of an E! News article about his original post.

“I promise you this was blown out of proportion,” he wrote. “I have a condo in Florida. I just didn’t want to leave PA because I fell in love with it.

“I was definitely sad and in shock. But I’m not destitute. Apologies for confusing wording in the moment.”

London initially sparked concern among fans about his employment and living situation on Thursday after sharing a post on X that has since been deleted.

entertainment.title: Before Gilligan's Island, Bob Denver Starred In A Beloved '60s Sitcom
entertainment.summary: Most people think Gilligan was Bob Denver's breakthrough TV role, but that's not actually the case. It was this beloved '60s sitcom that gave him his big break.
entertainment.body:
Airing from 1959 to 1963, the series followed the trials and tribulations of Dobie Gillis ( played by the late Dwayne Hickman ), an ordinary American teenager whose single-minded mission in life was simple: getting a girlfriend. The show's supporting ensemble included Frank Faylen and Florida Friebus as Dobie's parents, alongside future Hollywood legend Warren Beatty , who played Milton Armitage, Dobie's romantic rival. In a performance that surely paved the way for Gilligan, Denver injected some comedic energy into the lineup as Maynard G. Krebs, Dobie's jazz-loving, bongo-playing best friend. He also ha a famous catchphrase: whenever anyone talked about their job, he'd shout, "Work?!"

Of course, playing a beatnik meant that the clean-shaven Denver had to sport facial hair, which came with its own distinct set of challenges for the actor. Denver was not a fan of Maynard's trademark goatee. In a July 1962 interview with the Baltimore Evening Sun (via MeTV ), Denver went off about the personal and professional toll it took, sharing, "In over three years of playing Maynard on 'Dobie Gillis,' I haven't even been asked to play an outside role in another series or movie! And all because of this scraggly little beard." He added, "This beard gives me the type-casting-est face in Hollywood history. People spot me a mile away and mob me."

Decades later, fans of the show still hold the classic comedy in high regard, with the show sporting a solid 7.7 rating on IMDb. Reviewer laffinsal praised the series as "one of the high points of 1960s TV, and one of the most winning sitcoms of all time," adding that "Bob Denver is brilliant" as Maynard Krebs. User mcvouty78 wrote that "Bob Denver better deserves recognition for playing Maynard G. Krebs in this little gem of a series," and noted that Denver was :one of the first actors to show the TV audience that people can be hip and likable at the same time."

Following "The Many Loves of Dobie Gillis," Denver set sail for "Gilligan's Island," playing the titular role from 1964 to 1967. He later reprised his iconic role as the bumbling castaway in various "Gilligan's Island" TV movies and cartoon spin-offs throughout the 1970s and 1980s.

entertainment.title: How Trump Opened the Door for the Christian Left
entertainment.summary: James Talarico and Adam Hamilton ran on faith and won big. Democrats can thank the president
entertainment.body:
Two years ago, in the leadup to Kamala Harris’ failed run for president, I spent some time riding around Alabama and Georgia in a big blue tour bus with “Faith, Hope, & Love” plastered prominently along the side. The words come from a phrase in 1 Corinthians. The bus was being chartered by a group called Vote Common Good. The goal of Vote Common Good was to get people to vote for the candidates the group thought most likely to champion the common good — which just so happened to be Democrats, by and large. More specifically, the goal was to be achieved through chipping away at the idea that Republicans had a lock on godliness, that a Republican vote was, indelibly, a vote for God.

The bus was manned by a friendly crew of disaffected evangelicals, barefoot musicians, megachurch outcasts, and racial justice warriors who believed that the Black church in America had gotten politics right, that Jesus’ frequent admonitions to feed the hungry, clothe the poor, and love thy neighbor aligned more with a blue ballot than a red one. As a progressive Christian, I believed firmly in their mission, but I thought it was a mission at the margins. And in some ways, so did they. “We like to tell ourselves we are in a 40-year project,” Doug Pagitt, a Minnesota-based pastor and the organization’s executive director, told me at the time, before going on to explain that while he believed that even a slight change in Evangelical voting patterns could make a difference in some key districts, he had no illusions about wholesale change. It had taken decades to build the Christian Right’s voting bloc . Even Vote Common Good’s most ardent disciples thought they were in for a long slog through the wilderness before they reached anything close to the Promised Land.

Then came Tuesday’s election results and a parting of the Red Sea right up the I-35 corridor. James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas won their deep-red-state Senate elections in a landslide (by 12 and five points, respectively) in part because the Republicans deserved a reckoning, in part because Talarico and Hamilton were highly appealing candidates running against highly unappealing ones, and in part — large part — because their faith-based messaging found footing, especially in states where a majority of the population is church-going. entertainment.title: TVLine's Performer Of The Week: Paul Bettany
entertainment.summary: Paul Bettany wowed us with a quartet of performances this week on VisionQuest - see why he's TVLine's Performer of the Week.
entertainment.body:
Disney+ Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover THE PERFORMER | Paul Bettany

THE PERFORMANCE | We only have one column to honor the week's finest television acting, but we really ought to have four this time around: That's how many distinct roles Paul Bettany played during this week's "VisionQuest," a quartet of performances that totaled his best work in the Marvel series thus far.

Tuesday's penultimate episode forced Vision to confront the very intense, very human emotions that this version of the synthezoid has been avoiding all season long, finding them too painful to face head-on. But a poignant journey through Vision's psyche — if that's what you'd call it, anyway; the guy's an android — surfaced all of those pesky feelings at last. Along the way, Bettany not only portrayed the present-day Vision, but also the OG Vision who's been gone for years; J.I.M., the original Synthetic Man; and Dr. Phineas Horton, the Synthetic Man's creator .

It speaks to Bettany's talent that, in the episode's climactic scenes, we nearly forgot he was playing all four of those roles. Surely the actor performed against body doubles, green screens, and tennis balls on poles in order to bring this sequence to life, yet each synthezoid (and one human man) could be distinguished from the others thanks to subtle differences in their mannerisms and speech. This may not be Bettany's first MCU rodeo, but we still applaud how seamlessly he executed so many scenes opposite himself.

The emotional heft, though, came not from the post-production magic that put four Bettanys in a room together. Rather, it came from the wave of emotion that crashed over present-day Vision as he finally allowed himself to grieve both Wanda and his other son, Billy. Vision had successfully compartmentalized those (presumed) deaths for years, and when he sobbed, "I lost Wanda" over and over, an overwhelmed Bettany brought the appropriate magnitude to that moment of crushing clarity. Now more than ever, Vision is capable of genuine human emotions — and Bettany had us feeling a whole lot of those, too. — Rebecca Luther

Scroll down to see who got an Honorable Mention shout-out this week...

Hulu Sarah Paulson's unhinged, unpredictable performance as Carrington "Carr" Lane was the best reason to watch the first season of "All's Fair," and that continues in the Ryan Murphy legal drama's second season , of which the first three episodes are now streaming on Hulu. Episode 2 was a standout for Carr, who was begrudgingly invited to join the women as they scattered Dina's late husband's ashes in Martha's Vineyard. The catch? Carr is deathly afraid of flying! Liberty tried to slip her a Xanax, but we're sure glad the drinks got mixed up, because we can't imagine better in-flight entertainment than watching Carr lose her mind at 30,000 feet. There was a particularly funny running gag about Carr's many death-adjacent experiences, beginning with the time she (allegedly) missed her flight to New York City on September 11, 2001. Yes, that flight. Carr even claimed she was supposed to be on the infamous 1999 rollercoaster ride with Fabio when he was hit in the face by a goose, a line Paulson delivered with absolute sincerity. Intense turbulence shifted the mood of the flight, and Paulson suddenly took her performance from hysterical to heartbreaking as Carr left what could have been the final video message her daughter would ever see. Paulson's ability to balance Carr's cartoonish demeanor with her hidden humanity was a thrill to behold. Don't get us wrong, we're glad the plane landed safely and everyone survived, but with Paulson on board, we wouldn't mind circling a few more times. — Andy Swift

entertainment.title: Boston Blue's Gloria Reuben Worked With A Star Trek Actor On Alfred Hitchcock Presents
entertainment.summary: Before portraying the district attorney on "Boston Blue," Gloria Reuben acted alongside this "Star Trek: TNG" fan favorite in "Alfred Hitchcock Presents."
entertainment.body:
CBS Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Gloria Reuben was getting a first-hand look at criminals on "Alfred Hitchcock Presents" long before she was cast in the "Blue Bloods" spin-off "Boston Blue." One of Gloria Reuben's first acting roles was in the '80s reboot of "Alfred Hitchcock Presents," where she played Pam, a bank teller who unwittingly gives an unfaithful husband the cash he needs to arrange his wife's murder in the Season 2 episode "World's Oldest Motive." The husband in question was played by none other than Dwight Schultz, who portrayed the engineer Reginald Barclay in "Star Trek: TNG." While Reuben's Pam is initially unsuspecting of Schultz's character, David Powell, she becomes shocked after Powell's second thoughts about his crime cause him to behave in an erratic manner.

Both Schultz and Reuben appeared in "Alfred Hitchcock Presents" (one of the best anthology horror TV shows of all time ) at relatively early stages in their career. At the time of the episode's 1987 airing, Reuben was eight years away from being cast in "ER," where she made TV history as the HIV-positive physician assistant Jeanie Boulet. Schultz would later establish himself as a Trekkie fan favorite through his portrayal of Reginald Barclay, who reappeared a handful of times on "Star Trek: The Next Generation" after his 1990 debut. While the actors have not appeared onscreen together since their co-starring on their episode of "Alfred Hitchcock Presents," they both have gone on to find their own acting niches, with Schultz focusing largely on voice-over work and Reuben securing roles in TV dramas like "Mr. Robot" and "Boston Blue."

USA Network In the years since her work on "Alfred Hitchcock Presents," Gloria Reuben's evolving acting career has allowed her to seek out the characters that she finds most fascinating — and according to Reuben herself, the role of District Attorney Mae Silver on "Boston Blue" couldn't be a more perfect fit.

"[I]t was like Mae was written for me, in a way," Reuben told TV Fanatic in a May 2026 interview. To Reuben, Mae Silver's status as matriarch of the Reagan family on "Boston Blue" allows the actress to embody her principal values of "faith, family [and] service" — and it doesn't hurt that, unlike Reuben's role on "Alfred Hitchcock Presents," Silver wields an active authority in the crime-fighting process. "Playing a district attorney is the perfect thing for me, because I like to tell people what to do, and I think I'm always right," joked Reuben.

entertainment.title: Houndmouth’s Matt Myers No Longer Has to Be Sad to Write Great Songs
entertainment.summary: The leader of the Americana blues-rock band taps into a new feeling — reciprocated love — for the album Lordy : "It’s not that you have to be sad to create, but I’m happy at home"
entertainment.body:
It’s nearing the end of summer and Houndmouth lead singer and guitarist Matt Myers is walking up Main Street in Burlington, Vermont. Behind him is Waterfront Park where he’ll play later that evening opening for the Head and the Heart. He’s meeting up with family nearby for a quick bite and conversation with familiar faces amid a nationwide tour. With a few beads of sweat rolling down his neck, he stops on the corner of St. Paul Street, and starts to talk about falling in love.

“That changed everything. To finally be accepted, no matter what, by my wife and my friends,” the 38-year-old tells Rolling Stone . “Because I’ve always shown the same thing to people, and to get that reciprocated, that fucking rocks.”

Myers got hitched two years ago. It’s his second marriage, and he has two young daughters from the first. He’s found solace and balance in his life now, and it’s that harmony that provides the lyrical undercurrent of Lordy , Houndmouth’s new album. Released on Dualtone Records, it’s one of the centerpieces of the label’s 25th anniversary year.

For the indie-rocker, the record is about recognizing the face in the mirror and making peace with the eyes looking back at you. Nowadays, Myers is proudly acknowledging the salt and pepper in his hair, the well-earned wrinkles of tours across America and back again. It’s a long way from his baby-faced nature when he formed Houndmouth in 2011. But he’s OK with that, and with the fact that you don’t have to be sad to write great songs.

“I knew that it was a misconception, but you still can’t escape it sometimes,” Myers says. “It’s not that you have to be sad to create, but I’m happy at home. Now when I’m writing, the song doesn’t have to be grandiose. You don’t have to overthink. You can just write, edit, and then let the song be what it is.”

Myers still lives in the town where Houndmouth was conceived — New Albany, Indiana, situated right across the Ohio River from Louisville, Kentucky. That geographical and musical crossroads of the Midwest and the South has been an incubator for numerous rock acts who have emerged from the Louisville scene. Back then, Myers was doing “the standard cover band thing” at spots like Huber’s Winery and local bars. “You play for four hours and your fingers are just toasted. And then you try and throw an original song in and it never works,” Myers says. “So, eventually, I was just like, ‘I’m going to get my friends together. We’re only playing songs we write and we’re not making any compromises.’”

entertainment.body:
Premiering on HBO on March 12, 1995, "Happily Ever After" was a cartoon anthology series that retold classic fairy and folk tales in a multicultural setting featuring notable voice actors. Narrated by Robert Guillaume, the roster of guest performers included Harry Belafonte, Rosie Perez, James Earl Jones, Will Smith, Samuel L. Jackon, and New York City mayors Ed Koch and Rudolph Giuliani, to name a few. Washington appeared in two episodes, as King Omar in a season 1 retelling of "Rumpelstiltskin" and as Humpty Dumpty and the Crooked Man in a season 2 episode titled "Mother Goose: A Rappin' and Rhymin' Special."

"Happily Ever After" ran for three seasons, ending in 2000. A New York Times story from when the show premiered said the animation was just passable, but the instinct to reimagine European children's tales in diverse settings was admirable, and the stories were well-told.

HBO Denzel Washington's first major role was Dr. Philip Chandler on the acclaimed medical drama "St. Elsewhere," but he essentially left television behind when the NBC series ended in 1988. Since then, he's only narrated three PBS documentaries and directed a 2016 episode of "Grey's Anatomy." Those two voice roles on "Happily Ever After" are his only post-"St. Elsewhere" TV acting credits.

Until fairly recently, this wouldn't have been notable. For most of the medium's history, movie stars rarely appeared on television. Actors like Washington may have gotten their start on the small screen , but once he'd established himself as an A-list film actor, it would've been viewed as a step backward if he appeared in a TV show. Maybe you'd get an actor to pop into a recording booth for a day or two so they could voice a cartoon character, like in "Happily Ever After," but whenever a movie star appeared on TV in the flesh, it was a big deal.

That started to change with the streaming era, as prestigious limited series with big budgets drew Oscar-winning actors back to TV. Washington, however, never followed in the footsteps of Julia Roberts ("Homecoming") , Mahershala Ali ("True Detective") , or Nicole Kidman and Meryl Streep ("Big Little Lies") .

Now it seems as though "Happily Ever After" will officially be Washington's final TV acting role. During an interview with "Today" in 2024, he announced his intent to retire after he wrapped his final projects, and none of them were TV shows.

entertainment.body:
Natasha Wilson is seeking justice after a harrowing run-in with a dog.

In a lawsuit filed on Nov. 3 and obtained by E! News, the Lifetime star—who appeared in Single and Ready to Jingle , Trust in Love as well as the UnREAL series—said she has been unable to work in the two years since being bitten by a dog named Scruffy at a Los Angeles dog park.

She is suing the dog's owner Gregory Marcel , who she alleges did not have Scruffy on his leash and "could not promptly reach, control, or restrain the dog" when the animal approached her French bulldog on Nov. 7, 2024.

According to the complaint, Scruffy allegedly stood over Wilson's bulldog "in an aggressive and dominant posture" and jumped at the actress when she tried to intervene, knocking her to the ground.

Wilson then claimed that Scruffy continued to attack her while she was "on the ground attempting to shield her dog with her body and hands,” per the filing.

"During the attack, Scruffy bit [Wilson] on the face, above her right eyebrow," the lawsuit alleged. Upon seeking treatment at a local hospital, Wilson said she was diagnosed with a "facial laceration," prompting medical workers to irrigate and loosely suture her wound because of "the risk of infection associated with dog bites."

"As a result of the incident, [Wilson] suffered a laceration above her right eyebrow requiring sutures and has been left with a permanent, visible, and painful scar, an altered eyebrow hair pattern, hypersensitivity at the site of the wound, and impaired movement of the right brow," the suit read, alleging that she has also been "advised that she requires scar revision surgery and additional treatment."

Wilson said she now has permanent scarring above her right eyebrow as well as "shock and injury to her nervous system, all of which have caused "great physical, mental, and nervous pain and suffering, disfigurement, and emotional distress."

entertainment.title: 5 Cop Dramas That Were Canceled Too Soon
entertainment.summary: These short-lived cop dramas deserved better, but timing sometimes isn't right. Whether it was ratings or budget, these shows were canceled before their time.
entertainment.body:
FX Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover From "NYPD Blues" to "The Wire," many cop shows have enjoyed a long, successful place on television redefining what a cop drama should be , but some of them were short-lived, even though they deserved better. Cop shows have taken audiences by the hand and satisfied their appetite for the procedural and substantive aspects of law enforcement. The intersection of grizzly shootouts, department politics, and the personal lives of police officers makes for a unique, entertaining look at one of society's most dangerous professions.

It goes without saying that several shows fitting this description have aired over the years, but not all of them enjoyed as long a life as "CSI" or "Law and Order." Sprinkled throughout the history of cop shows are the ones that had great ambition, but never got the chance to fully blossom into what they could've been. In honor of those series that got the boot before they could reach their full potential, here is a list of five cop shows that were taken down far too early.

CBS/YouTube A one-season series, "Paris" featured James Earl Jones in his first television starring role as Woodrow Paris, a captain with the LAPD supervising a group of young detectives. Aside from his position as a police officer, the series also showcased his home life with his wife Barbara (Lee Chamberlin) and his second job as a criminology professor at a college.

This CBS series was conceptualized by legendary producer Steven Bochco, who would go on to develop procedural dramas like "L.A. Law" and "Hill Street Blues." Despite good reviews, the show was cancelled after airing only 11 of the pilot season's 13 episodes.

The behind-the-badge look at the main character's life outside the police department was not common for cop shows during this time. This is a structure that Bochco would implement in most of his work. Unfortunately, it was not enough to save the show with a 10:00 pm Saturday time slot . This was one of the worst times of the week to air a show. Most people were either in bed or out with friends at that time.

Fox Fox's two-season crime/psychological drama "Prodigal Son" featured Thomas Payne from "The Walking Dead" as Malcolm Bright, a former FBI profiler working as a consultant with the NYPD to solve crimes. On the show, Bright regularly consults with his incarcerated serial killer father, Dr. Martin Whitly (Michael Sheen), a former surgeon.

entertainment.title: Quote Of The Day By Denzel Washington: 'They Were Going To Pay Me A Lot Of Money And...'
entertainment.summary: He's amassed a considerable fortune, but to do so, Denzel Washington didn't have to compromise his artistic integrity or succumb to greed.
entertainment.body:
From "Remember the Titans" to "Malcolm X," Washington's filmography is stacked with several compelling watches. But let us not forget his impact on TV. He starred in NBC's hit medical drama "St. Elsewhere" and he also joined the set of "Grey's Anatomy" to direct an episode . He also indirectly saved one of TV's greatest cop shows – if it weren't for the positive reception to "Training Day" following the events of 9/11, FX's "The Shield" wouldn't have been greenlit.

In the past couple of years, Washington starred in "Gladiator II" and reunited with Spike Lee for their fifth collaboration, "Highest 2 Lowest." Although he can transform into any role, that doesn't mean that he will take on every script that comes his way. This Denzel Washington Quote of the Day shows he knows when to say "no" to a project that doesn't play to his strengths.

TVLine "They were going to pay me a lot of money, and I really thought about it, but I didn't do it."

The quote above comes from an interview that Denzel Washington gave for The Talks in 2012, where he spoke about passing on roles early in his career after Sidney Poitier's guidance. The "In the Heat of the Night" leading man told Washington that the first five films that you star in shape your trajectory as an actor. This advice prompted him to pass on an unmade comedy that would pay him a lot of money.

Washington thought the script was "terrible," but he did think about the offer for a while before declining it. The decision enabled him to later land a role in 1987's "Cry Freedom," the film that earned him his first Academy Award nomination. This experience even led Washington to relay advice of his own for young actors getting offered crummy, lucrative parts: "You don't have to compromise. Go do some theater and wait."

The film he mentioned in The Talks interview wasn't the only one he passed on. Washington reportedly turned down roles in "Se7en" and "Michael Clayton." He told GQ that he regretted passing on the latter, claiming that he was impressed by the script but was reluctant to work with a first-time director. In the same year that "Michael Clayton" was released, Washington starred in Ridley Scott's "American Gangster," which had a predominantly positive critical reception.

The clever way with which the actor has managed his career and trusted his gut instincts has allowed him to excel and become an influential name in Hollywood. As he prepares to star in "The Take," "Black Panther 3," and more "Equalizer" sequels, Washington has no plans to retire.

Benson Boone opened the Australian leg of his Wanted Man tour with a special guest. He brought a 13-year-old fan who is battling cancer onstage to sing “Beautiful Things” with him on her birthday. Explore Benson Boone See latest videos, charts and news

The moment came at the end of Boone’s set at Brisbane Entertainment Centre on Friday (Nov. 6). The Music reported that the singer stopped to introduce the final song. “I’ve had the opportunity of meeting a 13-year-old girl who is battling her second round of cancer,” Boone told the crowd, according to the outlet. “It’s her birthday today and her birthday wish was to come on stage and sing ‘Beautiful Things.’”

The fan, Kenzie Riddle, then rose from an upper platform and joined Boone on the song. According to The Music, roughly 10,000 people were in the arena.

Riddle has Ewing’s sarcoma. “Beautiful Things” was Boone’s breakout single. Released in January 2024, it reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the most-streamed songs in the world that year. entertainment.title: ‘Hold Onto Me,’ Cyprus’ First Oscar Hopeful, Stars a Newcomer and a ‘Dogtooth’ Actor in a Very Personal Father-Daughter Drama
entertainment.summary: Writer-director Myrsini Aristidou's feature debut, starring Maria Petrova and Christos Passalis ('Dogtooth'), tells the story of an 11-year-old girl whose father she has never known comes to town.
entertainment.body:
It’s summertime in Cyprus. Iris, 11, spends her days with her older best friend, Danae. But then she hears that her grandfather has died. Visiting town for his funeral is Iris’ father, Aris, whom she has never known. That is the starting point for Hold Onto Me , the feature debut of writer-director Myrsini Aristidou. Can Iris and Aris find a way to connect, even though he is a petty criminal and doesn’t want to take responsibility? Iris doesn’t give up and gets involved in his various schemes, despite warnings from her mother and her older brother. What begins as a stubborn attempt to reconnect slowly unfolds into a fragile bond. But then, Aris’ dark past gets them into trouble. Related Stories TV 'The Remarried Empress' Sets Disney+ and Hulu Record With Biggest Local Original Launch Ever Movies AFM Hot Project: Rosamund Pike to Star in Body Horror 'Feed'

Hold Onto Me , starring newcomer Maria Petrova and Christos Passalis ( Dogtooth ), premiered at Sundance, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic Audience Award. It then became Cyprus’ first-ever international feature film Oscar submission.

Now, the film screens in the Just Film youth and children’s event of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia. Cercamon is handling sales.

Lasse Ulvedal Tolbøll was the cinematographer on the Cyprus-Denmark-Greece co-production. The editors were Jenna Mangulad and Aristidou. Aristidou and Monica Nicolaidou produced the film, with Thomas J. Mangan IV and Mark Hollinger as the executive producers and Anders N.U. Berg, Konstantina Stavrianou and Rena Vougioukalou as co-producers.

Aristidou talked to THR about her bittersweet first feature, pairing an unknown as the young girl at the heart of it with the man who played the son in Dogtooth , her desire to make Hold Onto Me feel different and that first-ever Cypriot Oscar submission.

The father-daughter theme is one that the filmmaker has also explored in two shorts. “I feel like this is like a triptych,” Aristidou tells THR . “My first short film called Semele in 2015 is also a father and daughter story and was the first time that I began exploring this theme. Then I did my second short film, Aria , which has a father daughter dynamic again, but with an older daughter – she’s a teenager. They were short, and I wanted to go deeper in this subject matter.”

Hold Onto Me allowed her to do so in feature form, but she wanted it to be surprising and different from other films about similar familial relationships. “I wanted to use the archetypical relationship of father and daughter within a love story,” she explains. “It’s kind of a love story. It’s about two people who don’t know how to be together. They are sort of strangers in the beginning. They meet, then slowly come together, and they end up accepting each other or even loving each other in their own way. And when you set this up within the framework of a father, daughter and their family, it creates a different energy.”

entertainment.body:
A lot has changed for the Reagan brothers since we last saw them together on "Blue Bloods."

Season 2, Episode 5 of "Boston Blue" marked Will Estes' first appearance as Jamie Reagan since "Blue Bloods" ended its 14-season run in December 2024 — and his reunion with older brother Danny (Donnie Wahlberg) revealed that the distance between them wasn't merely geographical.

Now an NYPD lieutenant and a father to Joey Francis , Jamie arrived in Boston for a police conference harboring some resentment over Danny's decision to leave New York shortly after the birth of his and Eddie's son. (Eddie did not accompany Jamie to Boston, but sent her regards.) What began as a family visit soon turned into a joint investigation involving a diamond heist and a violent family feud, forcing the brothers to confront some lingering tensions of their own.

By the end of the hour, Jamie had come to understand why Danny needed to be in Boston for his son Sean, while Danny acknowledged just how much his departure had hurt his younger brother. Their reconciliation culminated in a heartfelt exchange, with Danny telling Jamie how proud he was of him — not just as a brother and a cop, but now as a father.

In the video interview above — a transcript is provided below — Estes reflects on revisiting Jamie, the real-life emotions behind his reunion with Wahlberg, an unexpected encounter with his former on-screen wife, Vanessa Ray, and whether he'd be open to returning to "Boston Blue."

No, it came about more recently than that. entertainment.title: Russell Brand’s jail hell revealed: Vermin-infested cells, violent inmates and drug searches
entertainment.summary: The comedian’s new reality behind bars comes with cramped living quarters, rampant violence, and a strict rules for loved ones hoping to see him.
entertainment.body:
Russell Brand is facing a grim reality behind bars at one of London’s most troubled prisons.

The “Get Him to the Greek” actor, 51, is being held at HMP Wandsworth following his conviction for rape and three counts of sexual assault . Inside, he faces a facility plagued by overcrowding, vermin and violence, according to official watchdog reports.

The Victorian prison is operating at 163% of its normal capacity, compared to a national average of 107%, according the Howard League for Penal Reform .

Wandsworth has 1,457 inmates despite having certified normal accommodation for just 894.

A 2024 report by Wandsworth’s Independent Monitoring Board painted an especially bleak picture of life behind bars, describing conditions inside as “inhumane” and warning of severe risks caused by overcrowding.

The report stated that two men were routinely required to share single-occupancy cells, with some described as “cramped, squalid and featuring broken or missing windows, furniture and fittings.”

Basic necessities were also in short supply, with inmates sometimes going two or three weeks without a full change of clothing. Showers were described as damp, unhygienic and insufficient in number, while poor ventilation allowed mold to return even after refurbishment.

The report also found that crumbling floors provided access for vermin, heating was intermittent because of frequently malfunctioning boilers and summer cell temperatures frequently topped 95 degrees Fahrenheit.

sports.summary: Rams safety Quentin Lake got plenty of attention for comments he made about intercepting a pass thrown by Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, but on reflection, Lake didn't like the attention he generated.
sports.body:
Lake told the Los Angeles Times that he reached out to Herbert to apologize.

On a podcast hosted by Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, Lake laughed about how confident the Rams were heading into the game with the Chargers, seeing how much Herbert has been struggling this season.

“He was throwing deli meat out there,” Lake said on the podcast. “He’s seeing ghosts. I don’t know what’s going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one.”

Lake and St. Brown were high school teammates, and Lake said that in the moment, he just felt like he was joking around with an old friend. When he saw how far his comments spread, however, Lake felt bad that he came across as disrespecting an opponent. Lake said he texted Herbert but hasn’t heard back from him.

“I don’t know if he read it,” Lake said. “He probably says, ‘I don’t care about it anymore. I’m not trying to see this. It doesn’t matter. You said what you said.’ But at the same time I . . . felt like it was right for me to at least say,’ Hey, man, I didn’t mean it in any disrespectful way .’”

Lake said he considers Herbert “a great quarterback” despite his struggles this season.

sports.title: Ravens reportedly tell Derrick Henry they have "no intention" of trading him
sports.summary: Ravens running back Derrick Henry's production has plummeted since quarterback Lamar Jackson was first injured before halftime in a Week 4 win over the Titans.
sports.body:
After Thursday night’s 33-10 loss to the Jaguars, a clearly frustrated Henry (who rarely displays frustration publicly), said he hasn’t mentioned going elsewhere as the trade deadline looms.

Now there’s this, from Adam Schefter of ESPN: “The Ravens recently informed Henry that they have no intention of trading him , according to league sources.”

If “no intention” is used in that assertion in the same way that multiple teams have used “no intention” in the past, a trade remains possible. Because intentions can change.

The Ravens traded for quarterback Jacoby Brissett in an effort to salvage a potential playoff season. Even after Thursday night’s game (which was only the second Jacksonville win in Baltimore since 2000), the Ravens are 4-5 and very much alive for a playoff berth.

In our view, the Ravens would trade Henry only if he made a passionate and compelling case to be traded — and if the Ravens are already considering moving on from the soon-to-be 33-year-old tailback after the 2026 season.

Henry has two former head coaches on current playoff contenders. Former Titans coach Mike Vrabel leads the 5-3 Patriots. Former Ravens coach John Harbaugh runs the 4-2-1 Giants.

The Patriots are without Treveyon Henderson, who will miss his second straight game after developing a sudden and unexplained illness. And the Giants have been linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.

So unless “no intention” means “no way,” it’s still a possibility. At least until 4:00 p.m. ET arrives on Tuesday.

sports.title: Report: Colts are in trade talks regarding QB Daniel Jones
sports.summary: The list of "multiple teams" currently includes the Ravens (who pivoted elsewhere) and the Vikings.
sports.body:
According to ESPNFL, the Colts have engaged in trade talks this week regarding Daniel Jones, speaking to “multiple teams.”

The precise language of the report identifies only one team as actually talking to the Colts. From the article, the Ravens “were one team to check in on Jones.” The Ravens ultimately struck a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, whose plunge from No. 1 to No. 3 on the depth chart made it clear to the rest of the league that he was available.

The only other team mentioned by name is the Vikings, and the report points only to "[s]peculation” involving Minnesota. (We’ve been “speculating” about it since the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s loss by the Vikings in Detroit.)

Past ESPNFL reporting on a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor ultimately listed five teams as talking to the Colts (Giants, Seahawks, Broncos, Packers, Vikings). The fact that other teams weren’t mentioned as to Jones suggests that, frankly, there may not be other teams.

Really, which current contender would want him? The Vikings are the only potential playoff team that checks the box as possibly needing a starter right now. And only the Vikings and Giants are contenders with which Jones has direct experience. (The Giants wouldn’t want a Jones reunion, and Jones surely wouldn’t want it, either.)

That could change this weekend, obviously. One injury to a starter could alter the dynamics, spurring another contender to pick up the phone and make a push for Jones. The most memorable example of that came 15 years ago, when a broken collarbone to Raiders quarterback Jason Campbell prompted a quick deal for Bengals quarterback Carson Palmer, who had decided he didn’t want to play for the team that had drafted him — and who had yet to report.

Three years ago, Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins popped an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline, forcing the Vikings to scramble at the deadline to do a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Josh Dobbs.

Absent a multi-week injury to a starting quarterback on a contender that doesn’t believe its backup can hold down the fort, the Vikings may be the only team that wants Jones at the deadline.

sports.body:
The Broncos have checked in with multiple teams about potential tight ends they could trade for, and that included the Cardinals, who told the Broncos they’re not interested in trading McBride , according to ESPN.

McBride is 26 years old and under contract through 2029, so it’s no surprise that the Cardinals see him as part of their future, although there’s never any harm in one GM calling another to see if a player is available. If the Broncos thought there was any chance they could get him, it was smart to ask.

The Broncos’ top tight end, Evan Engram, has just 13 catches for 136 yards this season. Sean Payton would love to get more production out of the tight end position than that. It won’t be a surprise if several more teams with potentially available veteran tight ends hear from the Broncos between now and Tuesday.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills are off to a great start, sitting at 6-1 atop the entire AFC. The Minnesota Vikings are also off to a great start, and they are second in the NFC with a a6-1 record, as they are currently tired with the San Francisco 49ers. The Vikings have the NFL’s best defense. The Bills have the NFL’s best offense. Something’s gotta give, as the move title suggests, and while I don’t expect to see Jack Nicholson in this one—or Diane Keaton, for that matter—I do expect to see a darn good football game. If the Bills are going to come out on top, they’ll need all of their top players to perform to their capability. Here are five Bills to watch on Monday night. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Josh Allen In a game like this, Allen has to avoid trying to do too much. Just take the checkdown. Take the easy money. Take the thing the defense gives you so that you can sustain the drive. Don’t come out juiced up trying to be a hero from the jump. Just play within the system, hit your keys, focus on your reads, and throw it to the guys wearing white helmets. If you do that, you’re probably going to leave Minnesota with a win. If you hold the ball, force it downfield into double coverage, and try to make chicken salad out of a far less desireable byproduct of chicken feed? Well, this is a defense that will make you pay. Allen doesn’t need to be Superman for the Bills to win on Monday. He just needs to be Josh Allen. RB James Cook III IF this stellar Vikings defense has a weakness, it’s the running game. They’re currently allowing opposing teams to average 4.5 yards per carry. That doesn’t bode well for the Vikings against the NFL’s third-best rushing offense. Cook averages 5.1 yards per carry this season, and Buffalo’s second-leading rusher—Allen—averages 4.9 yards per rush. If those two can take off, look out. The Bills worked Ray Davis into the rotation a bit more last week, which was nice to see. I’d like to see them do that a little bit more on Monday, as well, as Davis offers a different build and different running style to Cook. If Buffalo’s top back can find his footing, though, it will go a long way towards keeping the Bills on schedule, which will lead to points. sports.title: After career-low numbers in 2025, Justin Jefferson's production is even lower in 2026
sports.summary: Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson had his worst season in 2025.
sports.body:
Jefferson’s stats are actually worse across the board in 2026 than they were in 2025, when he seemed to have reached the bottom of what a player his caliber is capable of producing.

Last year, Jefferson finished with a career-low 1,048 receiving yards. This year, heading into Week 9, Jefferson has just 335 receiving yards.

Last year, Jefferson averaged a career-low 12.5 yards per catch. This year, Jefferson is averaging 12.0 yards per catch.

Last year, Jefferson had a career-low 47 receiving first downs. This year, Jefferson has 17 receiving first downs.

Last year, Jefferson averaged a career-low 4.9 catches per game. This year, Jefferson is averaging 4.7 catches per game.

Last year, Jefferson averaged a career-low 61.6 receiving yards per game. This year, Jefferson is averaging 55.8 yards per game.

The major question to ask is whether this means Jefferson has declined, or whether the blame goes to the Vikings’ quarterbacks who haven’t been able to get him the ball over the last two years. An answer to that question may come on Monday night against the Bills, when Carson Wentz starts in place of Kyler Murray, who has been announced as out with a hamstring injury.

Jefferson’s best game this year came in Week 1, when he had just two catches for 11 yards early on with Murray in the game, then caught six passes for 81 yards and two touchdowns from Wentz after Murray left with a concussion. Jefferson also had his best games last year catching passes from Wentz: Jefferson averaged 95.4 yards per game in the five games Wentz started in 2025, and averaged just 47.6 yards per game in the 12 games started by J.J. McCarthy and Max Brosmer.

sports.title: Myles Garrett: Rams' opponents will have to pick their poison, me or Aaron Donald
sports.summary: Garrett and Donald will play together for the first time on Sunday against the Commanders.
sports.body:
Donald did not play in Week 1 because he was still ramping up for the season after returning from his two-year retirement, and Garret hasn’t played since Week 1 because of knee surgery. Garrett said the two of them together, two multiple-time Defensive Player of the Year award winners side by side, will present a unique challenge for opposing offenses.

“I think offenses really have to pick their poison. Who’s going to be freed up this play? I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-one, so we’ll have some fun,” Garrett said. “Going into this season I never thought I’d have the chance, and as you all know he kept us in suspense for quite a while, so it was very exciting, and I’m looking forward to getting on the field and playing some real snaps with him.”

Garrett said his poor performance in Week 1 against the 49ers showed him he needed knee surgery, something he would have preferred to avoid.

“I was frustrated after the game. I knew that wasn’t me, and I was being hampered by something,” Garrett said. “I didn’t want to miss any time, but I had to be realistic about where I was physically, and I had to make the best choice for me and the team.”

But now Garrett is back, and he said he and Donald playing together can give the Rams an “elite defense” for the rest of the season.

sports.title: Patrick Mahomes is closing in on the record for most TD passes in a QB's first 10 years
sports.summary: Mahomes has 325 career touchdown passes, counting the playoffs. Peyton Manning had 327 in his first 10 seasons.
sports.body:
Mahomes, who is in his 10th NFL season, has 325 career touchdown passes, counting the playoffs. Only Peyton Manning, who had 327 touchdown passes in his first 10 years in the league, has had more.

So if Mahomes throws for two touchdowns on Sunday against the Jets, he’ll tie Manning’s record. With three touchdowns, Mahomes will have the record all to himself.

As a rookie, Mahomes played in only one game and didn’t throw any touchdowns. In the eight and a half seasons since then, Mahomes has 279 touchdown passes in the regular season, and another 46 in the playoffs.

Once Mahomes breaks the record, he’s likely to own it for a long time. The only active quarterback who’s closing in is Josh Allen, who is currently in his eighth NFL season and has 260 career touchdown passes. Allen has a chance of throwing for 68 touchdown passes in the next year and a half and moving ahead of Manning, but he’s highly unlikely to finish next season ahead of whatever Mahomes’ total is by the end of this season. This is a record Mahomes will own for a long time.

sports.title: The Vikings could be ready to make a trade for a quarterback, if they lose Monday night
sports.summary: Tuesday could become very interesting, absent a Carson Wentz-led win vs. the Bills.
sports.body:
This week’s apparent soft benching of Murray, who has a hamstring injury that possibly wouldn’t have kept him from playing if the Vikings had beaten the Lions on Sunday, gives Wentz a chance to beat the 6-1 Bills on Monday night. If he pulls it off, Wentz could keep the job for the remainder of the four-game gjallarhorn gauntlet that ends with trips to Wisconsin to play the Packers and Mexico to play the 49ers.

The Vikings will have roughly 16 hours after Monday night’s game ends to close a deal with another team for a quarterback. On Monday, we made the case for a trade for Colts quarterback Daniel Jones. As the week has unfolded, a variey of indications have emerged that it’s a real possibility.

Jones, who surely is dismayed by the Colts’ decision to prematurely throw in the towel by trading away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Bucker, would likely welcome the chance to return to a team with which he spent a couple of months in 2024 — and to lead the effort to propel the neo-Purple People Eaters to the postseason.

The other possibility would be to try to bring Kirk Cousins home. That would be more difficult. At 4-4, the Raiders are on the fringes of contention. Win or lose on Sunday at San Francisco, why disrupt something that’s working? Cousins currently ranks third in passing yards with 2,124 and second in touchdown passes with 19. His passer rating of 101.4 is higher than Josh Allen’s.

Even if the Raiders would be inclined to move Cousins and ride with Fernando Mendoza, it would cost far less to get Jones than it would to get Cousins. Especially since the Colts may already be planning to cut Jones before a $4 million roster bonus comes due in March and $6.51 million of his $33.49 million salary becomes fully-guaranteed.

With a new G.M. coming next year, why wouldn’t the Colts want a clean slate? Doing so would wipe out $38 million in non-guaranteed cash for 2027. Trading Jones would result in getting value; cutting Jones would get them nothing.

It may all come down to Monday night. If Minnesota wins, chances are nothing happens. If Minnesota loses, Tuesday could become a very interesting day.

sports.title: The Protect College Sports Act could be dead
sports.summary: This week's midterm elections will dramatically reshuffle the deck in Congress.
sports.body:
The last, best hope for a Congressional bailout to the college sports system (at the expense of the athletes in the revenue-generating sports) comes in the upcoming six-week lame-duck session. The bill has cleared the Senate. The House of Representatives, which disbanded in the middle of September to block a push for the impeachment of U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, has done nothing with it.

The question now becomes whether the short-timers in the House will muster the will to push their own version of the PSCA through to a successful vote.

Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas), who co-sponsored the original bill, seems to realize that if it doesn’t happen now it never will.

“There is no realistic path to secure the same broad bipartisan support for a new bill in 2027 and beyond,” a spokesperson for the Senate Committee on Commerce, led by Cruz, told The Athletic . “Passing the Senate-approved bipartisan bill through the House and sending it to the President’s desk during the lame duck Congress gives House Republicans an opportunity to close out the 119th Congress with a significant win for President Trump, HBCUs, women’s sports, and student athletes. An attempt to amend it would be a surefire defeat for the colleges and fans counting on PCSA’s enactment.”

At this point, do House Republicans want to give Trump a win? Right or wrong, those who won’t be coming back in January surely believe they lost their bids for re-election because of him. If so, they’ll feel no compulsion to spend time and effort on another presidential pet project at a time when the list of real issues that need to be addressed keeps growing.

If anything, the House would pass an amended version that would require reconciliation while the clock on the 119th Congress ticks toward midnight. The fact that the Senate Commerce Committee regards even an attempt to amend the existing bill as a “surefire defeat” for the bill will make the current House members who soon will be former House members even more likely to say, “Why bother?”

sports.title: Rams listed Matthew Stafford with elbow injury because reporters asked about ice on it
sports.summary: On Monday, reporters asked Rams coach Sean McVay about quarterback Matthew Stafford having ice on his throwing arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers.
sports.body:
“Really, it’s because you guys asked me about it earlier in the week,” McVay told reporters on Friday regarding the decision to disclose an elbow injury for Stafford. “It’s more semantical than anything else. It’s normal, like what he told you guys, but because you guys asked me about him having ice on his elbow. . . . He’s been full, hasn’t missed any sort of reps so normal management stuff that he’s been doing over the last few years.”

It conjures memories of the Patriots’ one-time habit of listing former quarterback Tom Brady as “probable” with a “right shoulder” injury. That all started because he had ice on his shoulder in the locker room, reporters inquired, and the team decided to just put him on the injury report every week.

“I haven’t seen any of that,” McVay said. “I told you guys he’d be better equipped to talk about it. He’s been a full participant, been awesome. He’s spinning the ball. He’s been able to activate all parts of the field with great timing, rhythm, and accuracy so he’s been great.”

So either he has an actual elbow injury that the Rams had been concealing, or he doesn’t really have an elbow injury but they listed him as having one because reporters noticed ice on his arm and asked McVay about it. Neither explanation seems to reflect the true spirit of the injury report, which expects real injuries — and only real injuries — to be disclosed.

Either Stafford has an elbow injury that was previously hidden or he doesn’t have an elbow injury and the claim that he has one is a middle finger to the meddling reporters who were doing their jobs. Neither explanation is a preferred alternative to the unvarnished truth.

sports.title: Saints to have "chip on our shoulder" after Browns' "chirping"
sports.summary: The Saints, like all teams, pay attention to the things said by their upcoming opponents.
sports.body:
Earlier this week, Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders seemed to make some less-than-flattering comments about the New Orleans defense. The New Orleans defense heard it, loud and clear.

“We’re gonna come in with a chip on our shoulder , for sure,” Saints defensive end Carl Granderson said Friday. “You know, they been chirping a little bit. We heard what the quarterback . . . said. So, you know, we’re [going to] come in hot and ready to play. . . . It’s gonna be a good game, for sure. We’re gonna come out with the [win].”

Asked Wednesday by reporters whether he has had a chance to study the Saints defense and to explain what he has seen, Sanders flashed a broad smile.

“Yeah, I’ve seen a lot,” Sanders said. “When I smile, just know that means something. I’m maturing. I’m maturing. Like, I could have given a decent answer, but now I’m just going to smile whenever it’s just, like, some questions.”

The better approach for Sanders would have been to project a poker face, and to give an answer that did nothing to attract the attention of the Saints’ defense.

So while he says he’s maturing, the ultimate level of maturity would consist of providing the most vanilla answer possible, praising the Saints and explaining that it will be a major challenge to beat them.

Instead, a Browns player has provided the next opponent — for the second straight week — with a little extra incentive.

sports.title: Drew Rosenhaus after Brandon Aiyuk's meeting with 49ers: "To be continued"
sports.summary: First session ends with no resolution.
sports.body:
It’s no surprise, then, that Friday’s sit-down between Aiyuk, agent Drew Rosenhaus, and the 49ers did not resolve the situation.

“Hey, guys,” Rosenhaus told a group of reporters who had staked out the Friday meeting. “ To be continued . We don’t have any further statements right now. But when we do, we’ll let you know.”

The situation seems pretty simple. Aiyuk arguably owes the 49ers upwards of $13 million. It’s one thing for the 49ers to have the ability to chase him around for the cash; it’s another for the NFL and the 49ers to delay his reinstatement to the league until he wires the funds.

That seems to be precisely where things stand. And the question becomes whether Aiyuk will be willing to strike a deal with the 49ers in order to secure the ability to return to the NFL, with another team.

sports.title: In defending his willingness to spend, Jerry Jones may have admitted to tampering
sports.summary: On Friday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tried to reverse the perception/reality that he deliberately underspends on coaches.
sports.body:
“I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on,” Jones said on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas.

Unless he was referring to college coaches (or high-school coaches), that’s tampering. Period. End of discussion.

It could be false — an effort to bolster the idea that, yes, he’s willing to spend. Still, the effort to put out the frugality fire he started on Tuesday by ridiculously claiming there’s no correlation between coaching pay and winning included a nonchalant concession that he has tried to pry NFL coaches away from their current teams, in blatant violation of the rules.

Will the NFL look into this one? Probably not. Because the league office surely realizes, as the rest of us do, that Jerry was simply saying whatever he had to say to lessen the impact of the accidental truth he told on Tuesday regarding a deliberate reluctance to do whatever he needs to do to make his team as good as it can be.

sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk: I’m back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated
sports.summary: The wide receiver and his agent are meeting with the 49ers about Aiyuk's future.
sports.body:
The wide receiver arrived at the team’s business offices in a van with his agent Friday afternoon to meet with the 49ers and presumably negotiate a resolution.

“Obviously, Brandon is here to meet with the team,” Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk’s agent, said before the meeting, via video from David Lombardi of the San Francisco Standard. “Fortunately, he’s feeling good physically. He’s healthy . He’s ready to get back to work. Don’t really have any comment about where he’s going to play. We’ll keep that between us and the Niners. But obviously we’re here with all the right intentions.”

Aiyuk last played in a game on Oct. 20, 2024, when he tore the ACL and MCL in his right knee. The relationship between the team and the player fell apart after that, and the 49ers voided the guaranteed money due to his unwillingness to rehab at their facility.

The 49ers placed him on the reserve/left squad list on Dec. 13, 2025. Rosenhaus filed a reinstatement request on Oct. 27, but the NFL still hasn’t reinstated him.

“Nice to see you all,” Aiyuk said. “I’m feeling great, feeling healthy. It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process. But I’m back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League.”

49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier in the day he "[couldn’t] care less” how the meeting went since “ it’s been over for our football team for a long time.”

That makes the session not a formal reporting-for-duty by Aiyuk, in the hopes of forcing the team’s hand. As explained earlier today, the NFL still hasn’t reinstated Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list — even though Rosenhaus filed the request on October 27.

Instead, it’s a meeting presumably aimed at negotiating a resolution to the situation.

The 49ers pushed to reporters on Thursday night the idea that Aiyuk’s return to the NFL is tied to the $13 million the team believes he owes in previously paid signing bonus. That shouldn’t be part of the analysis as to whether he’s reinstated by the league, whether the 49ers put him on the roster again, and/or whether the 49ers cut him.

But they’re making it an issue, because they can tie his ability to play to his willingness to wire the disputed funds to the team.

So that’s what’s happening. The brakes already have been applied to what should have been an administrative and automatic process. The league and the 49ers are working together to help the team get money back from Aiyuk before Aiyuk is permitted to get back into the league.

Then there’s the fact that an active arrest warrant is pending for Aiyuk, arising from a speeding incident. The business meeting could potentially be interrupted by an attempt to enforce a specific item of police business.

sports.title: Nick Sirianni admits that he misled reporters about quarterback situation
sports.summary: Instead of covering up one lie with another lie, Sirianni opted to tell the truth that he hadn't.
sports.body:
Because they all do. Particularly in so-called “must-lie” situations.

There’s an art to it. A way to conceal a lie with another lie. On Friday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted not to lie about the fact that he lied on Monday when he told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee would not be benched.

“ Tanner’s our guy ,” Sirianni said. “We’re not making any changes there.”

On Wednesday, the Eagles made a change there, elevating Joe Milton over McKee. The move was announced after Sirianni had his midweek media availability, which prevented him from being asked questions about the change in position from “Tanner’s our guy” to “Tanner’s not our guy.”

On Friday, Sirianni finally faced the music regarding his comments from Monday. In lieu of coming up with an explanation premised on the idea that what he said was true when he said it and circumstances changed, Sirianni surprisingly admitted that he wasn’t telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth to reporters and, in turn, the fans.

“I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute,” Sirianni said. “Again, I’m not real shy with you guys. I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y’all have to do, but I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I’m always going to protect the team first and foremost.

“Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there’s a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside.”

In an industry where the truth is only told when it’s coincidental to strategic interests, it’s jarring that Sirianni told the truth that he was lying. It would have been easy to say, “We took a more careful look at the situation after Monday.” Or, even more simply, “We changed our mind. Shit happens.”

sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings have been playing football against each other since 1971. But in more than five decades, they’ve met just 15 times. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings have been playing football against each other since 1971. But in more than five decades, they’ve met just 15 times. Minnesota holds a 9-6 advantage in the all-time series, although Buffalo has won four of the past six meetings. And, while there aren’t a whole lot of games to choose from, there are certainly a few worth remembering. There’s the afternoon Drew Bledsoe threw for more than 400 yards. The day a rookie Josh Allen introduced himself to the NFL by hurdling a linebacker. And, of course, there’s that game in 2022 that Bills fans would probably rather forget. So, before Allen heads back to Minnesota, we’re opening the Time Capsule to revisit five of the more memorable meetings between the Bills and Vikings, starting with a comeback in 1982. _____________________________________________________________________________ 1982 — A comeback worth remembering The Minnesota Vikings had a 19-0 lead over Buffalo on Sept. 16, 1982, and every reason to think they had the game under control. Joe Ferguson, however, had other plans. The Bills offense was a little late to the party, but it was about to make up for lost time. Ferguson threw for 330 yards and three touchdowns as Buffalo rallied for a 23-22 win. He got the Bills on the scoreboard with a 6-yard touchdown pass to Frank Lewis before halftime, then connected with Jerry Butler for a 4-yard score in the third quarter. Minnesota still held a 22-13 lead heading into the fourth, but a 21-yard field goal from Nick Mike-Mayer brought Buffalo within six. Ferguson and Butler connected again, this time from 11 yards out, and Mike-Mayer’s extra point gave the Bills the win. _____________________________________________________________________________ 2002 — An overtime shootout The Bills and Vikings combined for 78 points on Sept. 15, 2002, and somehow needed extra time and another six points to find a winner. Drew Bledsoe threw for a franchise-record 463 yards, but Buffalo needed a little last-second magic just to get the game into overtime. The Bills had taken a 36-32 lead on Bledsoe’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Peerless Price with 3:08 remaining, only for Minnesota to answer with a touchdown of its own and go ahead 39-36 with 26 seconds left. Bledsoe got Buffalo into position for a Mike Hollis 54-yard field goal as regulation expired. Then Bledsoe and Price delivered the finish.

sports.body: There’s finally a credible report on the Buffalo Bills’ intentions at the NFL trade deadline. John Wawrow of The Associated Press sent the following tweet on Thursday evening that features what we can safely assume is a paraphrased quote directly from Bills GM Brandon Beane: [Media: https://twitter.com/john_wawrow/status/2118484337947513027?a=H1QTu8Uyfh5KT1PAz0g&s=20] First off — good news for those who strongly believe the Bills should make a trade before the deadline on Tuesday, November 10. Secondly, targeting a defender makes plenty of sense and aligns with our trade deadline candidate serious here at Rumblings. At time of publication, the series has 10 installments, and eight of those articles have featured a defensive player. After the C.J. Gardner-Johnson release, it’d still be the easiest to assume Buffalo will target a veteran safety. They have loads of depth at the position right now. Some of that depth is young. Regarding the veteran reinforcements at that position, we’ll see if the Bills want to upgrade over Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone. Outside cornerback is also an option too despite the recently stable play from rookie Davison Igbinosun and Christian Benford returning to his super steady ways. Linebacker or even edge rusher aren’t out of the question either. Anticipation is building quickly, as the trade deadline is now only four days away.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills got an extra day of rest as they headed into Week 9 coming off a win over the Baltimore Ravens. With Week 9’s game against the Minnesota Vikings scheduled for Monday night, the Bills didn’t have an official on-the-books practice until today. And it may have helped things on the injury front. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2118462859717841260?a=5nhRoeOR_gSsQIG9KfY&s=20] Did not practice: * OL Alec Anderson * T Dion Dawkins * DL Greg Gaines * WR Joshua Palmer * RB Ty Johnson* Yes, there are two new names here, but I would expect both Anderson and Dawkins to be working by the end of the week. Maybe even tomorrow. There are a couple of key names not on this list to start the week, and that’s much, much better than the past couple of weeks. *Johnson just has an illness. Expect him back tomorrow. Limited Practice * T Spencer Brown * WR Keon Coleman * DB Jordan Hancock (IR) * TE Dalton Kincaid * WR DJ Moore Moore and Brown practicing today are good signs. sports.body: The Jets are on a three game losing streak that has dropped the team’s record to 2-6. The last two of the losses have come at home against beatable opponents. Unsurprisingly our latest SB Nation Reacts confidence poll suggests a majority of Jets fans do not feel good about the team. [Image: https://platform.ganggreennation.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/86/2026/11/Jets_1_110526.png?quality=90&strip=all] Interestingly, though, confidence actually edged up a bit. A week ago in the aftermath of the team’s loss to the previously winless Miami Dolphins, fan confidence fell to 21 percent. Our polls are not scientific, but I have to admit I am surprised to see around one-third of the fanbase still have confidence in the team’s direction. This might have to do with the rookie class looking solid and three first round picks on the way in. It almost certainly is not because of the level of coaching this team is receiving. In any event, I have seen a number of Jets seasons go off the rails in recent memory. Normally confidence is lower. We will see how this weekend’s game against the Chiefs impacts things.
